title: Embedded Finance, Open Finance and Big Tech Partnerships
summary: A nine-module programme for firms building embedded finance, open finance and platform partnerships, covering partnership models, responsibility, partner oversight, data sharing, customer outcomes and exit.
intro: This training programme equips payment, e-money, investment and fintech firms to build and run embedded finance, open finance and platform partnerships: choosing the model, allocating regulatory responsibility, overseeing partners and delivering good customer outcomes.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip firms that distribute through platforms, provide licensed services to partners or share data through APIs to grow these models without losing control of regulatory responsibility. Participants leave able to design a partnership model, oversee partners and data flows, manage dependency on large platforms and evidence to supervisors that the firm remains accountable for its customers.
sections.What It Covers: Platform economics and embedded finance models, choosing a partnership model, the regulatory perimeter and allocation of responsibilities, partner due diligence and oversight, APIs and open finance data sharing, financial crime and client funds across the chain, consumer outcomes in embedded journeys, operational dependency and exit, and governing and evidencing the partnership programme.
Intended Audience: Founders, chief executives, product and partnerships leads at payment, e-money, investment and fintech firms
Compliance, MLRO, risk, outsourcing and third-party risk staff overseeing partners and distributors
Technology, data and API leads responsible for open finance connections and platform integrations
Learning Objectives: Explain how platform economics and embedded distribution are reshaping financial services
Design a partnership model that allocates regulatory responsibility clearly along the chain
Oversee partners, agents and programme managers through due diligence, contracts and monitoring
Manage consent, security, liability and data protection in API-based data sharing
Deliver and evidence good customer outcomes, financial crime controls and client fund protection in embedded journeys
Manage dependency on large platforms and evidence accountability to supervisors
sections.Structure and Format: Nine modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with case studies and practical exercises, building to a partnership review workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of payments, e-money, investment distribution or fintech partnerships is helpful. No technical background in APIs is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FSB, Enhancing Cross-border Payments: Stage 3 Roadmap (2020)

modules.title: Platform Economics and Embedded Finance Models
modules.summary: How large technology platforms and non-financial brands enter financial services, the data, network and activity loop behind their advantage, and what this means for a licensed firm's strategy.
objectives: Explain the economics of platforms and the data-network-activities loop
Distinguish embedded payments, lending, investment and insurance distribution models
Assess where embedded and platform distribution creates opportunity and risk for the firm
syllabus: Network effects, ecosystems and cross-subsidisation
Big tech entry routes: own licence, partnership or acquisition
Embedded payments, credit, investment and wealth journeys
Strategic questions: grow, defend, partner or supply

modules.title: Choosing and Designing a Partnership Model
modules.summary: The main ways licensed firms work with platforms and fintechs, from white-label and agent arrangements to licence-as-a-service and API distribution, and how to select a model that the firm can genuinely control.
objectives: Compare white-label, agent, distributor, programme manager and licence-as-a-service models
Evaluate the commercial terms, control rights and risks of each model
Design a partnership model the firm can oversee with its current resources
syllabus: White-label, agents, distributors and introducers
Licence-as-a-service, e-money-as-a-service and middleware providers
Distribution through big tech platforms, marketplaces and super-apps
Pricing, revenue share and incentives that drive behaviour

modules.title: The Regulatory Perimeter and Allocation of Responsibilities
modules.summary: Where the regulatory perimeter falls when regulated and unregulated activities are combined in one journey, and how to allocate and document responsibilities so that the licence holder stays accountable.
objectives: Identify which activities in an embedded journey are regulated and who performs them
Apply activity-based and entity-based regulation to mixed-activity partnerships
Document responsibilities so that accountability cannot fall between partners
syllabus: Same activity, same risk, same regulation in practice
Perimeter traps: unlicensed activity, financial promotions and agency
Responsibility matrices and partnership mapping
Senior manager accountability for partner-delivered services

modules.title: Partner Due Diligence, Onboarding and Ongoing Oversight
modules.summary: How to select, onboard and monitor partners and programme managers proportionately, with the contractual rights, management information and escalation needed to act when a partner goes wrong.
objectives: Design risk-based due diligence and onboarding for partners
Specify contractual rights to information, audit, step-in and termination
Monitor partners through management information, testing and periodic review
syllabus: Partner risk assessment and onboarding criteria
Contracts: service levels, audit access, step-in and exit
Monitoring, assurance testing and partner management information
Case studies: fast growth, weak oversight and partnership failure

modules.title: APIs, Open Finance and Data Sharing
modules.summary: How open banking and open finance frameworks enable customer-permissioned data sharing, and how a firm designs consent, security, liability and data protection when it provides or consumes data through APIs.
objectives: Explain the design of open banking and open finance frameworks
Implement consent, authentication, security and liability arrangements for data sharing
Assess the strategic value and risks of data access for the firm
syllabus: Open banking to open finance: scope, data categories and participants
APIs, standards, consent dashboards and strong authentication
Data protection, fraud and cyber risk in data sharing
Data as a strategic asset: reciprocity and platform data advantages

modules.title: Financial Crime and Client Funds Across the Chain
modules.summary: How AML/CFT, fraud and sanctions controls and the protection of client funds work when onboarding, transaction monitoring and reconciliation are shared between the licence holder and its partners.
objectives: Allocate customer due diligence, monitoring and reporting duties between partners
Design fraud and scam controls for embedded and API-driven journeys
Ensure client funds are safeguarded and reconciled across the partnership
syllabus: Reliance, outsourcing of customer due diligence and digital identity
Transaction monitoring, sanctions screening and suspicious activity reporting
Fraud, mule accounts and authorised push payment scams on platforms
Safeguarding, client money and reconciliation with partner ledgers

modules.title: Consumer Outcomes in Embedded Journeys
modules.summary: How platform design, personalisation and frictionless journeys shape customer decisions, and how the firm tests and evidences fair outcomes, suitability and complaints handling when a partner owns the interface.
objectives: Identify harms from choice architecture, dark patterns and frictionless credit
Apply disclosure, product governance and suitability in partner-owned journeys
Design outcome testing, complaints handling and redress across the chain
syllabus: Choice architecture, defaults and dark patterns
Embedded credit, buy now, pay later and investment nudges
Personalised pricing, profiling and fair treatment
Complaints, redress and outcome monitoring across partners

modules.title: Operational Dependency, Concentration and Exit
modules.summary: How reliance on platforms for distribution, cloud, data and customer interfaces creates operational dependency and bargaining weakness, and how the firm builds resilience and credible exit options.
objectives: Assess the firm's dependency on platform partners and technology providers
Apply operational resilience and third-party risk management to partnerships
Design credible exit and contingency plans for critical partnerships
syllabus: Distribution dependency and loss of the customer interface
Cloud, data and technology dependencies on platform groups
Mapping partners to important business services and impact tolerances
Exit planning, substitutability and customer migration

modules.title: Governing and Evidencing the Partnership Programme
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a governance model for the firm's partnerships, from board risk appetite and management information to the evidence a supervisor will expect, ending with a partnership review workshop.
objectives: Set risk appetite and governance for growth through partnerships
Specify management information and assurance across the partner portfolio
Evidence to supervisors that the firm remains in control of its customers
syllabus: Board risk appetite, partner limits and approval of new partnerships
Portfolio management information and early warning indicators
What supervisors look for in thematic reviews of partnerships
Workshop: reviewing an embedded finance partnership through a supervisor's eyes
